scope: Deepen and broaden open-source peer evidence, validate exact release-versus-proposal boundaries, screen BRL-CAD as a possible ACIS route, and refine existing implementation owners without promoting support.

method.kind: Primary project documentation/source and issue-status review plus local plan cross-check
method.mutableSourceLimit: Current project pages and issue states are discovery evidence. ACadRust candidate commits were not built or independently retested; private issue corpora are unavailable. Any future comparator must bind exact source/release, toolchain, route, and inputs.
method.evidenceBoundary: Peer issue reports, proposed fixes, project documentation, and mapping references guide test selection but do not establish local defects or libdxfrw support. Unicode mapping files provide expected byte-to-scalar values for their named code pages; they do not establish which DWG/DXF label a producer uses.

evidence.topic: Legacy code-page peer failure and mapping authority
evidence.observed: ACadRust issue #131 supplies literal legacy byte decoding/encoding repros and says the same mapping table is used on both sides; maintainer commit 9f3a8b5 asks the reporter to retest, while the issue remains open. Unicode's published mapping files give stable exact expected byte-to-scalar values for CP437/CP850 and Apple Roman. Microsoft identifies codepage 1361 as Johab and 10000 as Mac Roman.
doesNotEstablish: that the candidate ACadRust change was independently retested or shipped in a particular package
the correct DWG/DXF codepage-label admission policy for every producer
that naming two codecs the same makes a read/write self-round-trip correct
evidence.planUse: Keep under PAR-05/Slice 3; use official named mapping tables for local wire-byte assertions, split alias selection from mapping and reverse encoding, preserve explicit unavailable behavior for Johab until a validated multibyte decoder exists, and use only the existing focused codec-test owner.

evidence.topic: Orphaned DWG ownership and phantom geometry
evidence.observed: The open peer issue reports 10 model-space entity-count discrepancies in 351 private DWGs and describes one AC1032 case with 51 entities from a dimension block whose owner record was missing being rehomed into model space. The author describes phantom dimensions; the maintainer proposed commit b62555f and requested a corpus retest. The corpus and independent retest are unavailable.
doesNotEstablish: a reproduced libdxfrw behavior or defect
a normative DWG rule for every orphaned owner class
the correctness of the peer candidate fix
that the existing DXF adapter orphan controls prove DWG parser recovery
evidence.planUse: Retain the existing PAR-49/7G.3 owner categories and generated DXF adapter tests. Keep a distinct DWG-origin orphan-with-suffix control on the composed owner gate; do not invent model-space ownership or infer erased-dimension semantics from unavailable private files.

evidence.observed: BRL-CAD is a mature open-source solid-modeling kernel and documents DXF conversion into BRL-CAD geometry. Its current development TODO still lists a SAT importer as work to implement; the reviewed documentation does not establish an available SAT/SAB reader. The separate dxf-g importer has an open issue reporting an ASan heap over-read from hostile POLYFACE indices.
doesNotEstablish: an existing BRL-CAD SAT/SAB importer or ACIS profile
a reproduced libdxfrw defect from issue #228
safety of sending malformed data to dxf-g
full DXF graph, DWG, ACIS-carrier, or native-CAD parity
evidence.planUse: Exclude BRL-CAD from ACIS semantic qualification until a real importer exists and is pinned/qualified. Do not run hostile vectors through dxf-g. Preserve only an optional valid explicit-mesh projection check after a fixed safe revision is established.

evidence.topic: FreeCAD route and supported consumer boundary
evidence.observed: FreeCAD's documentation repository is archived by GitHub as of 2026-04-01; the reviewed preferences page identifies itself as updated for version 1.0. It documents distinct C++ and optional legacy Python DXF import/export backends, with different feature and licensing characteristics. The described DWG route uses an external converter followed by a selected DXF importer; the documentation describes 2D scope and inability to read the proprietary ACIS solid payload.
doesNotEstablish: the current behavior of any specific installed FreeCAD binary or its default backend/settings
which backend or converter an unpinned run selected
ACIS solid semantics or ACDS attachment
that converter loss is a libdxfrw loss
evidence.planUse: Retain separate pinned Linux/Windows consumer cells for converter, intermediate DXF, selected importer, settings, and observed 2D entity semantics. Do not treat stock FreeCAD as an ACIS semantic oracle.

affectedOwners: PAR-05 / Slice 3 legacy-codepage mapping and wire policy
PAR-49 / 7G.3 DWG/DXF ownership and orphan disposition
external peer/kernel admission and FreeCAD native consumer profile
implementationReadiness.validationBudget: Only a touched strict build, one focused existing test owner, and git diff --check for a future local implementation slice. Keep peer builds and native/kernel runs at existing composed checkpoints; no per-slice full-suite expansion.
implementationReadiness.fixturePolicy: Use locally authored in-memory byte/record controls. Do not add or download third-party DWG/DXF/SAT/SAB fixtures in this research update.
